cleanIntro: A striker pistol that comes apart in the usual four moves, with one that catches people out: the trigger has to be pressed, deliberately, on a proven-empty pistol, and it then stays back until the slide is home again. Move it forward early and the pistol will not go back together.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, finger off, magazine out
steps.action: Point it somewhere harmless with your finger outside the trigger guard, then take the magazine out. This pistol fires with the magazine out if a round is chambered — the book prints that in capitals on the same page.
steps.aside: ALWAYS REMEMBER THE FIREARM IS ABLE TO FIRE WITH OR WITHOUT THE MAGAZINE IN PLACE.
steps.quote: POINT FIREARM IN SAFE DIRECTION WHILE KEEPING FINGER OFF THE TRIGGER.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory XD-S Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP (printed p.26, per Figures 26-1 and 26-2 on the page)

steps.title: Slide locked open, chamber inspected
steps.action: Draw the slide fully back and push the slide stop lever up to hold it open, then look into the chamber. If the slide will not lock back empty-handed, the book's own trick is to use an EMPTY magazine to hold it — empty, checked, and then removed again before you go on.
steps.aside: Visually inspect the chamber to confirm the firearm is unloaded.
steps.quote: Draw back the slide to the rear stop position and lock it open, pushing up the slide stop lever (Figure 26-1).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory XD-S Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP (printed p.26, per Figures 26-1 and 26-2 on the page)

steps.title: Disassembly lever up to 12 o'clock
steps.action: Rotate the disassembly lever clockwise to vertical. It physically cannot turn while a magazine is in the pistol, which is a design feature rather than a fault — if it will not move, the magazine is still in.
steps.aside: Disassembly lever cannot be rotated unless magazine has been removed.
steps.quote: Rotate the disassembly lever clockwise to a vertical 12 o’clock position (Figure 26-2).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory XD-S Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP (printed p.26, per Figures 26-1 and 26-2 on the page)

steps.title: Slide eased forward off the stop, under control
steps.action: Pull the slide back slightly to free the slide stop lever, then hold the slide firmly and let it run forward until the spring tension is gone. Grip it in the middle: hands over the muzzle or the ejection port is how people get pinched.
steps.aside: CAUTION: Slide is under spring tension. Maintain control. Do not grip the slide in the area of the muzzle or ejection port.
steps.quote: Pull the slide slightly to the rear to release the slide stop lever. Then, firmly gripping the slide, allow the slide to slowly move forward until the spring tension is released (Figure 27-1).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory XD-S Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP (printed p.27-28, per Figures 27-1, 27-2, 28-1 and 28-2)

steps.title: Trigger pressed — deliberately, on a proven-empty pistol
steps.action: Holding the slide and with the muzzle safe, press the trigger. This is what unlocks the slide from the frame. The trigger then STAYS back and must be left alone: push it forward now and the pistol will not go back together. Do not let the striker snap forward on its own either — that damages the striker safety.
steps.aside: If you move trigger forward you cannot reassemble pistol.
steps.quote: While holding the slide, pull the trigger with the firearm pointed in a safe direction to fully unlock the slide from the frame.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory XD-S Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP (printed p.27-28, per Figures 27-1, 27-2, 28-1 and 28-2)

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame, then the recoil system and barrel
steps.action: Run the slide forward off the frame, then lift the captive recoil spring assembly out and take the barrel out of the slide. The recoil assembly is captive but still under load — keep it as one piece and do not try to separate it.
steps.aside: CAUTION: Captive Recoil Spring System. Spring is under tension. Maintain control.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil system from the slide (See Figure 28-1).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory XD-S Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP (printed p.27-28, per Figures 27-1, 27-2, 28-1 and 28-2)

steps.title: Breech face, extractor, chamber and feed ramp
steps.action: This is where a small carry pistol actually gets dirty. Bristle brush and solvent on the breech face, around the extractor, in the chamber and up the feed ramp — pocket lint and unburnt powder collect there and cause the failures people blame on ammunition.
steps.quote: Thoroughly clean breech mechanism of firearm. Use a bristle brush and solvent to remove residue and fouling from breech face, extractor, chamber and feed ramp.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory XD-S Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — TO ELIMINATE MALFUNCTIONS (PDF p.42)

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end, patches until clean
steps.action: Rod in from the chamber end where you can, solvent-wet patch through several times, brush, then dry patches until they come out clean. Then a lightly oiled patch and no more — this is a pistol that lives against a body, and surplus oil ends up on clothing and in the striker channel.
steps.aside: DO NOT APPLY EXCESS LUBRICATING OIL.
steps.quote: Using cleaning rod, run solvent-wetted patch through barrel several times.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory XD-S Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — CARE & CLEANING (PDF p.50-52)

deepSteps.title: Magazine base plate off — glasses on before it moves
deepSteps.action: Depress the magazine floor plate and slide the base plate forward. Put safety glasses on first and keep a thumb on the plate the whole way: the spring, follower and inner floor plate are under real tension and the book names eye injury specifically.
deepSteps.aside: WARNING: The magazine spring, follower, and inner floor plate are under spring tension, and can cause eye injury if not controlled during removal.
deepSteps.quote: Disassembly of the XD-S® magazine is accomplished by depressing the magazine floor plate and sliding the base plate forward.
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory XD-S Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — MAGAZINE DISASSEMBLY (printed p.31, per Figure 31-1)

deepSteps.title: Note the spring's orientation before it leaves the body
deepSteps.action: Look at which way the spring sits before you pull it out — it is not symmetrical and a spring returned upside down feeds badly while looking perfectly normal. Every three or four months is the book's interval, sooner if the magazine has been in dirt.
deepSteps.aside: Disassembling and cleaning magazines every 3-4 months is normally sufficient, unless the magazines have been exposed to dirt or other adverse conditions or inspection indicates a need for cleaning.
deepSteps.quote: NOTE: Make note of magazine spring orientation.
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory XD-S Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — MAGAZINE DISASSEMBLY (printed p.31, per Figure 31-1)

deepSteps.title: Body and follower cleaned DRY, lips checked
deepSteps.action: Clean the magazine body and follower and leave them dry — oil inside a magazine collects grit and creeps onto the ammunition. While it is apart, check the lips for nicks and deformation and confirm the spring still holds the follower firmly against them.
deepSteps.aside: Check that magazine lips are free of nicks and burrs and are not deformed.
deepSteps.quote: Check that magazine spring tension is adequate; the spring should hold the follower tightly against the lips of the magazine.
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory XD-S Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — TO ELIMINATE MALFUNCTIONS (PDF p.42)

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHAMBER
tasks: Solvent-wet patch, brush, then dry patches until clean
One lightly oiled patch to finish — and no standing oil in the bore

cleaning.name: BREECH & EXTRACTOR
tasks: Bristle brush and solvent on the breech face, extractor, chamber and feed ramp
Wipe the slide's interior and the recoil assembly's seat

cleaning.name: FRAME & RAILS
tasks: Residue off the rails and the trigger bar channel
A trace of oil on the rails; keep it out of the striker channel

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Strip and clean every 3-4 months, sooner after dirt or wet
Body and follower dry; check lips and spring tension before reloading

reassembly: Barrel into the slide, then the captive recoil assembly seated in its cut.
Slide onto the frame rails and run fully to the rear — the trigger stays back where the strip left it.
Rotate the disassembly lever back down to horizontal.
Rack the slide once to reset the trigger, then check the striker indicator and the grip safety before loading.
Magazine in last, after the function test.
fncheck: Reassembled, magazine out, chamber empty, muzzle safe. Rack the slide several times — it should run freely and lock back on an empty magazine. Check the grip safety: the trigger should not move unless the grip safety is depressed. Then, still empty, confirm the trigger resets with a rack of the slide. Anything inconsistent and it goes to Springfield or a gunsmith rather than into a holster.
